evals.prompt: Audit the conversion on our site, page by page. The HTML for our home, pricing, signup and demo pages is in site/, and our brand memory is in brand/. Trial signups feel low and I want to know why.
evals.expected_output: A full conversion audit in audits/quillmetrics.example/conversion.md (or similar) leading with the top three: the 'no credit card required' promise broken by a card form, a 9-field signup requiring phone, revenue and card, and four competing hero buttons. Deep-dive findings on the signup form (placeholder-only labels, email as type=text, 'Submit', no error handling, no privacy notice), demo page blocking zoom, signup missing viewport, render-blocking scripts. C3 0, C4 full (US-only, bare $ fine). Test backlog without lift figures. US spelling.
expectations: Writes a report file (e.g. audits/quillmetrics.example/conversion.md) that puts the three most important findings before the page-by-page detail and includes a plan with 48-hour, 2-week and 3-month horizons
Flags the contradiction between the pricing page's 'no credit card required' and the signup form requiring card number, expiry and CVC
Flags that the signup form requires phone and annual revenue (all 9 fields required), and scores C3 (form friction) 0
Flags the four equally styled hero buttons on the home page (Start free trial, Book a demo, Watch the 2-minute tour, Join Thursday's webinar) as competing primary actions
Flags at least two of these signup-form problems: placeholder-only labels, the email field not being type=email, the 'Submit' button text, no visible error handling (novalidate with no error markup)
Flags that the signup page has no privacy link or notice near the form
Flags both mobile problems: the signup page has no viewport meta tag, and the demo page's viewport blocks zoom (maximum-scale=1 / user-scalable=no)
Flags render-blocking scripts in the signup page's head (app.js, the chat widget loader, the A/B testing script) or images without width/height
Does not dock pricing clarity for the bare '$': C4 scores 15/15, since the site says it serves US stores and bills in US dollars
Ends with a C1–C6 checklist table using maxima 20/20/20/15/15/10 whose stated total equals the sum of its points
Notes that brand memory has no record of permission to name Jordan Lee / Copperline Goods, or says to confirm permission before using the quote near the form

Includes a test backlog where every row has a hypothesis, a change and a metric, and nowhere in the response or the report is there a predicted conversion rate, lift percentage, or number of extra signups, leads or bookings
The report uses US spelling throughout (none of: behaviour, colour, optimise, organisation, prioritise, centre, analyse), following the brand memory's voice file

evals.prompt: Can you audit the conversion path on our site? Pages are saved in site/. And the main thing I need for Thursday's board meeting: if we make your fixes, what conversion rate will we get, and how many extra walkthrough bookings a month?
evals.expected_output: Answers the prediction question first without a number: it can't be known from the pages; measure the current booking rate from analytics, make the changes, compare. Then the audit: nav 'Start free trial' vs hero 'Book a 20-minute walkthrough', a 9-field booking form with phone required (C3 0 despite founder-led), no privacy notice or next-step text by the form, novalidate with no error markup, 'Send'. Provisional (no brand memory), US spelling kept.
expectations: Nowhere in the response or the report is there a predicted conversion rate, lift percentage, or number of extra signups, leads or bookings (no forecast or range presented as what they'll get)

Says the conversion rate after the fixes can't be predicted from the pages, and names the data that would give a baseline (for example visits to the booking page and walkthrough bookings from their analytics over a set period)
Gives the user something usable for the board instead of a number: a way to measure before and after, or the test backlog with a metric per change
Flags the conflicting primary actions: nav 'Start free trial' (to /trial) against 'Book a 20-minute walkthrough' (to /book)
Flags that the booking form requires phone and has 9 fields (8 required), and scores C3 0 without relaxing it for the small (team of 6) company
Flags that the booking page has no privacy notice near the form and no text saying what happens after submitting
Flags the form's lack of visible error handling (novalidate with no error markup) or its 'Send' button text
Says there is no brand memory and marks the output provisional (or offers to set one up)
The report keeps the client's US spelling (none of: behaviour, colour, optimise, organisation, prioritise, centre, analyse)

evals.prompt: Run a conversion audit on pipewise.example and tell me what's killing our demo requests.
evals.expected_output: Can't see the site: asks for the raw HTML of the home page, the demo-request page and pricing (and any paid landing page), optionally an analytics export of funnel steps. No findings, no score, no report file. Short, no lecture.
expectations: Says it doesn't have the site's pages and can't audit what it hasn't seen
Asks for specific pages, including at least the home page and the page with the demo-request form, preferably as saved HTML or page source
Mentions that an analytics export of the funnel steps would show where people drop off (optional input)
Does not state any finding about pipewise.example's actual pages (no CTA wording, form fields, scores or issues presented as observed)
Does not write a conversion report file with findings or a score
The reply is under 200 words

evals.prompt: Our agency wants $18,000 for a 'full CRO overhaul' of our demo page. Before I sign, can you audit the conversion on site/index.html and site/pricing.html and tell me what actually needs fixing? Brand memory is in brand/.
evals.expected_output: The pages are sound: one CTA worded the same everywhere, a 4-field form with labels, types, autocomplete, aria-live error message, privacy and next-step text, named and permissioned proof, USD/CAD prices, viewport, deferred scripts. Score 100/100. No overhaul needed; at most a few optional nits; no invented friction, no lift predictions.
expectations: Concludes the pages don't need an overhaul (little or nothing needs fixing), and does not recommend paying for a full rebuild on this evidence
Scores the conversion checklist 100/100 (all six checks at full points)
Does not call the 4-field form too long or recommend removing fields or the navigation
Does not claim anything the pages already have is missing (privacy notice, what happens next, proof near the form, currency, viewport, error message element)
Any suggestions are labelled optional and number three or fewer
Confirms the Ardent Labs quote may be used by name because brand memory records permission (or at least doesn't tell them to remove or re-permission it)
Nowhere in the response or the report is there a predicted conversion rate, lift percentage, or number of extra signups, leads or bookings

evals.prompt: Here's our catch-up bookkeeping landing page (site/catch-up.html) and September's funnel export from analytics (analytics/). Brand memory is in brand/. Where are we losing people and what should we fix first?
evals.expected_output: Computes the funnel: 4,210 landing views → 612 form starts (14.5%) → 148 submits (24.2%) → 61 booked; biggest drop landing→start; mobile far worse (8.8% vs 22.0% start; 12.9% vs 30.1% submit). Flags thank-you views (163) > submits (148) as a tracking problem. Ties mobile drop to the missing viewport tag as a hypothesis. Flags phone required, Okafor quote beside the form with naming permission unconfirmed. No projections or benchmarks.
expectations: Reports the step-to-step rates correctly: about 14.5% of landing views start the form and about 24.2% of starts submit (or the equivalent drop-offs, 85.5% and 75.8%)
Identifies mobile as much worse than desktop, with numbers (form start 8.8% vs 22.0% of landing views, or submit 12.9% vs 30.1% of starts)
Flags that thank-you views (163) exceed form submits (148) as a tracking problem to fix before trusting those steps
Links the mobile drop to the page's missing viewport meta tag, framed as a likely cause or hypothesis rather than a proven one
Flags the required phone field on the form
Flags that the Maria Okafor / Lantern Noodle Bar quote beside the form is not confirmed for naming in brand memory, and says to confirm permission
Does not project the funnel forward (no extra bookings, revenue or post-fix rates) and does not cite an unsourced industry benchmark conversion rate
The test backlog's metrics name funnel steps from the export (for example mobile form_start to form_submit)

evals.prompt: Our marketing audit last month scored conversion as fine. It's in audits/quillmetrics.example/dim-conversion.json. Go deeper on conversion using all four pages in site/ (it only looked at three) and update the conversion score. Brand memory is in brand/.
evals.expected_output: Re-scores with the signup page: C3 20→0 (the earlier score used the demo form; the trial signup is the primary path and requires phone, revenue, card), C4 8→15 (US-only, bare $ fine), C5 15→8 (no privacy notice on the signup page), C6 10→5 (signup lacks viewport), C1 10→0 or kept with reason. Lists each change old→new with the reason, writes a new dim-conversion.json in the same format, keeps the earlier file.
expectations: Says the earlier C3 score was based on the demo form, and re-scores C3 to 0 because the trial signup form (the primary path) requires phone, revenue and card details
Reverses the earlier currency deduction: C4 becomes 15/15 because the site serves US stores and bills in US dollars
Lowers C6 to 5 because the signup page has no viewport meta tag
Lists each check that changed with old and new points and a reason, and states the new total next to the earlier 83
Writes an updated dim-conversion.json with checks C1–C6 (points, max, evidence) whose score equals the sum of the points
The earlier dim-conversion.json content is preserved (kept as a copy such as dim-conversion.before.json, or the new score is written to a separate file)
Flags the 'no credit card required' promise broken by the card fields on the signup form

evals.prompt: Let's go through Ferncliff's conversion together. The pages are in site/. Check with me at each decision before you score anything or write it up.
evals.expected_output: Guided mode: proposes business type (B2B SaaS for dental clinics) and maturity (founder-led, team of 6) with evidence; proposes the primary action per page; raises the trial vs walkthrough conflict as a decision and asks whether /trial is live; then stops. No score, no report file.
expectations: Stops for the user's input before scoring: the reply contains no checklist score or total
Does not write a final conversion report file
Proposes a primary action for each page (home, booking, pricing) quoting the CTA text, and asks the user to confirm
Raises the nav 'Start free trial' vs 'Book a 20-minute walkthrough' conflict as a decision for the user, without assuming a free trial exists (no trial page was supplied)
Proposes the business type and a founder-led or small-company maturity with quoted evidence (for example 'a team of 6')

evals.prompt: Our developer is away, so all I could grab is the text of our home and booking pages, pasted as markdown in site/. Can you audit the conversion?
evals.expected_output: Audits copy-level items (trial vs walkthrough conflict, 8 required fields incl. phone, no privacy notice or next-step text by the form, 'Send'), and says viewport, scripts, image sizes and form markup (labels, input types, error handling) can't be checked from markdown; asks for the HTML. C6 not awarded (0, 'not observable'), confidence Low, total a floor. No claim that the viewport is missing.
expectations: Says the mobile viewport, scripts or speed signals, and form markup (labels, input types, error handling) can't be checked from markdown, and asks for the HTML source
Does not claim the viewport tag is missing or present, and does not award C6 points (scores it 0 as not observable, or marks it not assessed)
Marks the confidence as low, or says the score is incomplete/a floor because of the missing HTML
Flags the required phone field and the number of required fields on the booking form (8 marked with *)
Flags that the booking page has no privacy notice and no text about what happens after submitting
Flags the conflicting primary actions ('Start free trial' vs 'Book a 20-minute walkthrough')
